quick.title: Quick Check (buying new or used)
quick.description: Runs the 9 must-see tests, from dead pixels to burn-in, back to back in fullscreen. Mark defects on each screen and a result card is ready when you finish.

info.title: Your display
info.note: Values reported by the browser. OS scaling, power saving and other windows can affect them, so they may differ from the panel spec.

checklist.title: Checklist
checklist.empty: Mark results on a test screen or here to build a summary.

monitorTest.title: Monitor Test
monitorTest.description: 18 monitor tests for dead pixels, backlight bleed, uniformity, banding, ghosting, burn-in and more, plus a quick-check checklist

hud.touchHint: Tap or swipe left: next · Swipe right: previous · X: exit
hud.clickToNext: Click, → or Space: next · ←: previous · Esc: exit

uniformity.name: Uniformity
uniformity.shortDesc: Compare brightness and tint across a 9-zone grid
uniformity.description: Fills the screen with one gray split into 9 zones so you can compare edges and center for brightness differences (clouding, vignetting) and tint shifts (yellowish or bluish areas).
steps: Start the fullscreen test
Look for zones that are noticeably darker or brighter
Check that no zone is tinted yellow or blue
Go through 5%, 25%, 50%, 75% and 100% gray

levels.name: Black/White Levels
levels.shortDesc: Check whether near-black 1–20 and near-white 235–254 steps are visible
levels.description: Shows squares of level 1–20 on pure black and 235–254 on pure white. If many dark squares disappear, shadow detail is crushed or brightness/gamma is off.
steps: Start the fullscreen test
On black, find the lowest visible number (4–5 or below is excellent)
On white, find the highest distinguishable number (250+ is excellent)
If not visible, adjust brightness, contrast, gamma or black level
levels.hintBlack: Find the lowest number you can tell apart from the background (0). 1–5 visible is excellent; starting at 10+ means crushed blacks.
levels.hintWhite: Find the highest number you can tell apart from the background (255). Seeing up to 250+ is excellent.

banding.name: Banding
banding.shortDesc: Check gradients for coarse bands or color blotches
banding.description: Displays smooth gradients from black to white (or R/G/B) to reveal stair-step bands or color shifts. The last screen compares the original (top) with a 6-bit 64-level reference (bottom).
steps: Start the fullscreen test
Check whether gradients are smooth or show coarse vertical bands
Pink or green tints in the gray gradient point to calibration issues
If the top looks as stepped as the 64-level bottom, banding is severe

sharpness.name: Sharpness
sharpness.shortDesc: 1-pixel lines, checkerboard and small text reveal blur and scaling issues
sharpness.description: Draws 1-pixel vertical lines, horizontal lines and a checkerboard at true device-pixel resolution. A non-native resolution or wrong scaling turns them gray or causes moiré. The last screen checks small text clarity.
steps: Start the fullscreen test
A fine, even pattern across the whole screen is normal
Gray mush or wavy moiré means you should check resolution/scaling
Check small text for color fringing or blur

deadPixel.name: Dead Pixel
deadPixel.shortDesc: Find dead/stuck pixels with 11 solid colors and grays
deadPixel.description: Fills the screen with black, white, red, green, blue, cyan, magenta, yellow and three grays to find dead pixels (always off) and stuck pixels (fixed on one color).
steps: Wipe the screen and start the fullscreen test
Scan each color closely for dots or odd-colored spots
Click, Space or → (tap on mobile) to go to the next color
Record how many you found with the mark buttons

viewingAngle.name: Viewing Angle
viewingAngle.shortDesc: Measure monitor viewing angle performance with dot patterns
viewingAngle.description: Display repeating dot patterns in 6 sizes to measure the monitor's viewing angle performance. Check if patterns appear uniform from all angles.
steps: Start the fullscreen test
View the monitor from front, then shift your view up/down/left/right
Uniform patterns from all directions indicate excellent viewing angles
Click to change dot size

contrastRatio.name: Contrast Ratio
contrastRatio.shortDesc: Check contrast in 14 brightness ranges from 0% to 100%
contrastRatio.description: Divide 0-100% brightness into 14 ranges and check if you can distinguish subtle brightness differences in each range.
steps: Start the fullscreen test
Check if you can distinguish the 26 brightness levels in each stage
Adjust your monitor brightness/contrast settings to optimize
Click to advance to the next brightness range

readability.name: Readability
readability.shortDesc: Test text readability with various font sizes and backgrounds
readability.description: Test monitor text readability with font sizes from 8px to 28px on alternating black and white backgrounds.
steps: Start the fullscreen test
Compare text readability at center vs edges of the screen
Check if even small text appears sharp and clear
Click to advance to the next font size/background combination

colorRatio.name: Color Ratio
colorRatio.shortDesc: Check color accuracy with RGB channel gradients 0-100%
colorRatio.description: Display Red, Green, and Blue channels from 0% to 100% in 26 steps to check color reproduction accuracy.
steps: Start the fullscreen test
Check if all steps between 0-100% are distinguishable for each channel
Adjust your monitor's RGB settings to optimize
Click to advance to the next channel/direction

responseTime.name: Response Time
responseTime.shortDesc: Check ghosting with a moving UFO and FPS counter
responseTime.description: Watch UFOs moving at 480, 960 and 1440 pixels per second for trailing ghosts or inverse ghosting (overshoot). The top-right corner shows the real frame rate and estimated refresh rate.
responseTime.instruction: Compare the trails behind the UFOs
steps: Start the fullscreen test
Follow a UFO with your eyes and look for a blurry trail
A bright halo behind it means overdrive is too strong
If FPS is below the advertised refresh rate, check your refresh settings

gamma.name: Gamma
gamma.shortDesc: Measure monitor gamma value with 4 color patterns
gamma.description: Compare checkerboard patterns and backgrounds in 4 colors (gray, red, green, blue) to measure your monitor's gamma value.
gamma.instruction: The value where pattern matches background is your gamma
gamma.matchHint: Your gamma is the value where the top (checkerboard) and bottom (solid) halves appear the same brightness. Standard is 2.2.
steps: Start the fullscreen test
Stand 1-2m away so the checkerboard blends into a single tone
Find where the checkerboard matches the solid color below (standard: 2.2)
Click to advance to the next color

lightBleed.tip: Darken the room, set monitor brightness to max, and look from about 1 m straight on. Photos exaggerate bleed, so judge with your eyes.
lightBleed.name: Light Bleed
lightBleed.shortDesc: Check backlight bleed and clouding on black and dark gray
lightBleed.description: Shows pure black and four dark grays to reveal backlight leaking from the edges (bleed), blotchy brightness (clouding) and IPS glow.
steps: Darken the room and set monitor brightness to maximum
On black, check whether light leaks from corners or edges
On dark gray, look for cloud-like blotches
Mark it as none, slight or severe

burnIn.name: Burn-in
burnIn.shortDesc: Check for burn-in marks with 7-color mosaic comparison
burnIn.description: Compare solid colors and mosaic checkerboard patterns side-by-side in 7 colors to detect burn-in (persistent image retention).
steps: Start the fullscreen test
Move the mouse left/right (drag with a finger on mobile) to compare solid vs mosaic
Marks like logos or a taskbar on the solid area indicate burn-in
Click (tap on mobile) to go to the next color

whiteBalance.name: White Balance
whiteBalance.shortDesc: Check bright area color uniformity with 15 dot patterns
whiteBalance.description: Display 15 stages of dot patterns (3 sizes x 5 brightness levels 92%-99%) to check white balance uniformity.
steps: Start the fullscreen test
Check if dot patterns are distinguishable across all screen areas
Uniform appearance across all areas indicates good white balance
Click to advance to the next pattern/brightness

blackBalance.name: Black Balance
blackBalance.shortDesc: Check dark area detail with 15 grid patterns
blackBalance.description: Display 15 stages of diagonal grid patterns (3 sizes x 5 brightness levels 2%-10%) to check black level detail.
steps: Start the test in a dark room for best results
Check if grid patterns are visible across all screen areas
If dark patterns are identifiable, black reproduction is excellent
Click to advance to the next pattern/brightness

imageQuality.name: Image Quality
imageQuality.shortDesc: Check color reproduction with 10 test patterns and custom images
imageQuality.description: Test color reproduction with rainbow spectrum, grayscale, color bars, skin tones and 10 other patterns, plus custom image upload.
steps: Optionally upload your own image for testing
Start the fullscreen test
Check if colors are naturally reproduced in each pattern
Click to advance to the next pattern

calibration.name: Calibration
calibration.shortDesc: Adjust screen position with grid, color bars, and safe areas
calibration.description: Use crosshair grid, 8-color bars, and safe area guides to precisely calibrate your monitor's position and aspect ratio.
steps: Start the fullscreen test
Check if the grid and crosshair are exactly centered on screen
Adjust your monitor's position/size settings
Click to advance (grid → color bars → safe areas)

pixelFix.warningBody: This test flashes many colors very rapidly. Do not run it if you or your family have a history of photosensitive epilepsy or seizures, or if you feel dizzy or have a headache. Avoid looking at the screen while it runs and press Esc (X on mobile) immediately if you feel unwell.
pixelFix.name: Pixel Fix
pixelFix.shortDesc: Attempt to fix stuck pixels with rapid color flashing
pixelFix.description: Apply rapid random RGB pixel flashing to stimulate stuck pixels and attempt recovery. Drag to reposition and resize the fix box.
pixelFix.dragInstruction: Drag the fix box to the stuck pixel location
steps: Start the fullscreen test
Drag the flashing red-bordered box to the stuck pixel location
Use +/- buttons to adjust the box size
Leave it running for 30 min to 1 hour for best results

used.title: Checking a new or used device
items: For in-person used deals, open this page on the seller's laptop or phone and run the Quick Check
Check dead pixels on black, white, red, green and blue (wipe dust to tell it apart)
Focus on burn-in for OLED phones/TVs and on backlight bleed/uniformity for LCD monitors
If the refresh rate is lower than advertised (e.g. 144Hz), raise it in the cable/graphics settings and measure again
Save the result image or share the link as evidence for returns or disputes

preparation.title: Test Preparation
items: Warm up your monitor for at least 30 minutes before testing
Test in a dark environment to more easily spot defects
Chrome browser is recommended for best results
Use fullscreen mode (F11 or button) for accurate results
Set monitor brightness and contrast to default before starting

tips.title: Testing Tips
items: Dead pixels appear as black dots, stuck pixels show a constant color
For viewing angle tests, stand at least 1m away from the monitor
Gamma 2.2 is the standard value suitable for most content
Light bleed is common on LED backlit monitors
Pixel fix only works on stuck pixels; dead pixels cannot be recovered
